findings.heading: Major revisions
findings.proposition: Version 1.0.1 of the handbook was released on 20 November 2022.
findings.reader_consequence: The Vietnamese revision table ends at the 10 May 2021 v1.0.0 release, so a reader believes the handbook has had only one release and cannot tell which version the text they are reading corresponds to.

findings.heading: Major revisions
findings.proposition: Version 1.0.1 implemented a listed set of changes: update to R 4.2; data cleaning switched {linelist} to {matchmaker} and removed an unnecessary line from the case_when() example; dates switched {linelist} guess_date() to {parsedate} parse_date(); pivoting updated pivot_wider() id_cols=; survey analysis switched plot_age_pyramid() to age_pyramid() and changed the alluvial plot code; heat plots added ungroup() to the agg_weeks chunk; interactive plots added ungroup() to the agg_weeks chunk so expand() works; time series added data.frame() inside all trending::fit() and predict() calls; combinations analysis switched case_when() to ifelse() and added optional across() code; transmission chains updated to a more recent {epicontacts}.
findings.reader_consequence: The whole NEWS block is absent from the Vietnamese chapter, so a Vietnamese reader does not learn that guess_date() was replaced by parse_date(), that {linelist} was replaced by {matchmaker}, or any other v1.0.1 change, and may follow superseded code from other chapters without knowing it changed.

findings.heading: Editorial decisions
findings.proposition: lubridate was chosen for epiweeks because of its flexibility (English), not because it is easy to read (translation).
findings.reader_consequence: A Vietnamese reader learns the wrong selection criterion for date handling: readability rather than flexibility, so when judging an alternative package for epiweeks they weigh the wrong property.

findings.heading: Editorial decisions
findings.proposition: The rationale for choosing incidence2 and ggplot2 for epidemic curves is dependability.
findings.reader_consequence: The Vietnamese cell reads "tuy theo" (it depends), which states no rationale at all, so a reader cannot see why these two packages were selected over EpiCurve and may read the row as an unresolved choice.
